newsitem.title: PERU: 80 hurt as Lima street vendors riot.
newsitem.headline: 80 hurt as Lima street vendors riot.

text.p: More than 50 security officers and 30 street merchants were hurt early on Sunday in a riot that erupted when city workers moved in to tear up a road in central Lima, city officials and news reports said.

Arturo Moreno, a spokesman for the city's security force, told Reuters close to 1,000 vendors, backed by "agitators and common criminals," threw stones and set fires in a clash with 300 municipal officers in the city's historic downtown.

Local television showed security officers dressed in riot gear squaring off with stick-wielding rioters, some perched on rooftops, throwing stones and running down streets illuminated by burning shops near Lima's central market.
"They threw back tear-gas canisters and shots were fired," Moreno added, without saying who fired the shots.
Four officers were seriously hurt, suffering broken bones and concussions. Local radio said at least 30 merchants also were injured in the clash.
TV station Frequencia Latina said several firefighters also were hurt.
"We were beginning remodeling work to restore the historic centre when informals (street vendors), armed with gasoline, attacked the municipal workers," Moreno said.
Vendors were cleared out of the area several days ago, he said, as part of the municipality's effort to clean up and rehabilitate the centre of this 562-year-old former Spanish colonial capital.
The riot broke out at about 2 a.m. (0700 GMT) when workers moved two machines in to begin tearing up the street and lasted about three hours.
